summary.one_liner: Broot is an interactive terminal tool for navigating directories, finding files, previewing them, and launching commands without losing sight of the file hierarchy.
summary.what_it_does: Broot shows a condensed, filterable tree view of a directory, hiding unlisted and gitignored entries by default, with toggles for hidden and gitignored files. Typing letters fuzzy-filters entries, and prefixes like "/" (regex) and "c/" (file content search) plus logical operators narrow results. Alt+enter opens the shell in the selected directory, so it can be used to cd. It can preview files (with image display in Kitty-protocol terminals), move, copy, delete and create files, run verbs such as opening an editor, use side-by-side panels, sort by size or date, show filesystem usage, and display git status and branch information. The README describes these features only briefly and points to external documentation for details.
use_cases: navigate directories quickly from the terminal
find files by name or regex
cd to a directory I only partly remember
replace ls or tree with a richer directory view
search file contents across a project
check git status of files in a repo
find what takes up disk space
how_to_run: Hit `br -s` to get an overview of a directory
Use `br -sdp` to show sizes, dates and permissions
Use `br --sort-by-size` or `br --sort-by-date` to sort on launch
notable: Alt+enter returns to the shell in the directory you navigated to
Content search with c/ prefix and combinable logical operators
Side panels for copying or moving files between directories
Git status view with branch and ahead/behind info
Image preview in terminals supporting Kitty's graphics protocol
caveats: Image preview requires a terminal supporting Kitty's graphics protocol (README names Kitty and WezTerm)
Installation and full documentation are only linked externally, not described in the README
